title: Normalized below-level derived scalar comparison
statement: Let $J,O,\ell,B_n$ and $\mathsf S_B$ be an essentially small site, a ring with an element, its constant quotient ring sheaves and their strict semilinear systems [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-strict-extension]. Fix ordinary extensions $E_n\dashv e_n$ with normalized comparisons $E_ne_q\cong T_{nq}$ for $q\leq n$. Fix arbitrary universal derived scalar adjunctions $LT_{nq}\dashv R_{nq}$ and universal pointwise derived evaluation adjunctions $LE_n\dashv e_n$, with their counits and evaluation localization factors [lem-pur-coefficient-scalar-derived-adjunction, lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-core]. Then $LE_ne_q\cong LT_{nq}$. On every complex $P$, the inverse isomorphism followed by $e_q$ applied to the extension counit, the evaluation localization factor and the localization of the ordinary below-level comparison is exactly the scalar counit. The formula holds without a K-flatness restriction.

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p. 21: the functors e_n! and (Le_n!, e_n^-1), with indices shifted from n >= 0 to n >= 1. The natural sigma maps are the truncation inclusions in its explicit formula; the Hom identity specifies their adjunction mates.

proof.text: Derived evaluation is a right adjoint, hence preserves all existing limits. The core left derived functor is pointwise, so postcomposition by this evaluation preserves its right Kan extension.

Conjugate the input functor by the evaluation localization factor and the termwise ordinary tensor comparison. Uniqueness of left derived functors gives the comparison with the prescribed scalar derived functor. Its universal counit equation, precomposed with its inverse, is the asserted representative equation.

theorem coefficientEvaluationDerivedBelow
    (ordinary : CoefficientOrdinaryEvaluationData (J := J) (O := O) (ell := ell))
    [∀ n, (ordinary.extension n).Additive]
    (scalar : CoefficientScalarDerivedAssignment (J := J) (O := O) (ell := ell))
    (core : CoefficientEvaluationDerivedCoreData ordinary) {n q : ℕ} (h : q ≤ n) :
    ∃ i : core.derivedExtension n ⋙ core.evaluation q ≅ (scalar h).derived,
      ∀ P, i.inv.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫
        (core.evaluation q).map ((core.counit n).app P) ≫
        (core.evaluationFactors q).hom.app
          (((ordinary.extension n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map
          ((NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex (ordinary.below h) (.up ℤ)).hom.app P) =
          (scalar h).counit.app P
